title: Selected Work
subtitle: Consumer mobile shipped with measurement, internal tools shipped without ceremony, and design owned end to end — problem to production code.

bio.short: I own problems end to end — PM, PO and designer in one seat for a consumer app redesign across iOS, Android, web and connected TV. The AI feature whose entry point I redesigned is in production, and its weekly starts more than doubled on iOS. I prototype in real code against production APIs, and engineering ships from that code.
bio.long:
At Bibel TV I am the product manager, product owner and designer for the app redesign in one seat — the purpose of the contract. The KI Bibelaufschlag AI feature I carried is live on iOS and Android: redesigning its entry point from an unclear button to a self-explaining input more than doubled weekly starts, +153% on iOS and +85% on Android, GA4 four-week averages around each release. Alongside it I ship internal AI products: a support copilot for the viewer-services team where every send decision stays human, and design infrastructure — a four-tier token API and a colour engine — that keeps four platforms in step.

At ChurchDesk I delivered a booking capability in two months on a €20k client budget — the deal closed before I joined; I led the delivery — embedded in the platform's existing calendar and form builder instead of the standalone module that was floated. 70% less coordination time and 90% acceptance at the launch customer, then rolled out to the whole base. The product ran under GDPR plus church data-protection law across six countries, and customers met the European Accessibility Act deadline automatically on the sites they host. Earlier, the mobile checkout I designed at HairDirect produced the company's first mobile orders.

I don't hand engineering a spec — I hand them something that already runs. I prototype in Claude Code against production APIs, web first, then continued natively in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose because Android is where most users are. Engineering at an external agency — outside my company entirely — reviews and ships from that code; a teardown of the shipped build verified 91.8% of the design-token fields and 94% of the core data model carried through. Before that, at Ninox, I designed the prompt-to-database AI onboarding with the CEO and technical co-founder: chat beside direct manipulation, so people edit what the model built.

context.emphasis: End-to-end ownership of loosely defined problems — discovery through shipped, run independently (PM, PO and design in one seat). Consumer mobile work that is live and measured, with the measurement method named (GA4, four-week averages around each release, feature-level). Design that survives contact with engineering: prototypes in real code that an external agency evaluates and ships from. Internal AI products shipped small and honestly scoped — a copilot that is one tool for one team, every send human. Rule-bound design under real constraints: a European Accessibility Act deadline met across six countries, GDPR plus church data-protection law, a two-month commercial envelope met. Process adapted to the risk and reversibility of each decision.
